Purpose: Wave 4 Pharmacy architecture, security, and migration design validation
UnsupportedAssumptions: No commercial Pharmacy application, vendor support matrix, or schema was supplied.
Windows Server EC2 compatibility and sizing are unverified.
RDS for SQL Server edition, version, collation, SQL Agent, licensing, and driver compatibility are unverified.
Provider endpoint, authentication, certificates, allowlists, retry semantics, and SFTP need are unknown.
Private clinic connectivity, controlled provider egress, and required SSM interface endpoints are not evidenced.
RPO 15 minutes and RTO four hours are design assumptions, not approved clinical requirements.
Directory authentication and DNS integration require validation before selection.

Architecture.ApplicationTier: Private Windows EC2, no public IP, no inbound RDP, IMDSv2, encrypted gp3 EBS, Session Manager administration through external endpoints
Architecture.DatabaseTier: Private Single-AZ RDS for SQL Server Express, db.t3.small, encrypted gp3, automated backups, final snapshot and deletion protection
Architecture.DatabaseFlow: Application security group to database security group only on TCP/1433 with TLS required at the client
Architecture.ProviderBaseline: Controlled outbound HTTPS API with idempotency, bounded retries, timeout handling, audit correlation, and reconciliation
ProviderAlternatives: Authenticated callback through a separately designed ingress boundary
SFTP with host-key pinning only when required by the vendor
Architecture.IdentityOwnership: External owner-controlled least-privilege roles and instance profile
Architecture.SecretOwnership: External Secrets Manager metadata and value lifecycle; Terraform receives ARN contracts only
Architecture.KmsOwnership: External governed KMS key ARN contract

SecurityControls: No public EC2 or RDS address
No IAM role or secret resource ownership in the module
Encrypted EC2, RDS, log, and backup storage
RDS automated backup, AWS Backup design, final snapshot, deletion protection, and prevent_destroy
Externally governed Session Manager, telemetry, KMS, secret, backup, and alert dependencies

BackupRestoreDesign.Validation: Restore to isolated validation boundary, verify integrity and control totals, then reconcile synthetic prescription and audit records

SyntheticScenarios: Provider success, failure, timeout, and unknown result

KnownWarnings: Sandbox cannot read the user-level Terraform CLI directory; formatting and validation still returned exit code 0.
Existing Appointment API DynamoDB hash_key and range_key arguments are deprecated.

CostConsiderations: RDS for SQL Server license-included runtime
Automated backup, AWS Backup, and snapshot retention
Interface endpoints if a future design supplied private service access
NAT Gateway or Transfer Family only if an evidenced provider requirement justified their fixed cost

BLOCKER: No vendor application, support matrix, schema, or integration contract exists in project evidence.
The evidenced private subnets have no SSM or provider egress path beyond the S3 gateway endpoint.
DESIGN REQUIREMENT: Keep RDS private and scope TCP/1433 to the application security group only.
Use Session Manager without routine RDP and supply exact external IAM, secret, KMS, backup, and alert dependencies.
Validate TLS, restore integrity, prescription audit data, and reconciliation before acceptance.
DESIGN CONSTRAINT: Single-AZ is a cost-conscious portfolio pilot and not a production availability recommendation.
Directory authentication, private client connectivity, and FSx need remain unverified.
COST CONSIDERATION: SQL Server licensing and Windows runtime are primary recurring drivers.
NAT, Transfer Family, and interface endpoints add fixed hourly cost and remain absent unless requirements justify them.
FOLLOW-UP: Obtain vendor, provider, clinical-owner, audit-retention, RPO, RTO, authentication, and network-path requirements before any future implementation design.
